City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 7, 2021
   City Council Special Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, December 7, 2021

  •  CALL TO ORDER
  •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Liao
  •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Liao, Vice Mayor Ding, Council Members Harrington,
  Menchaca, Pu

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. COMMENDATION FOR 2021 OUTSTANDING OLDER AMERICAN SALLY
  BALDWIN

  B. EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION AWARDS

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of November 16, 2021.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 16, 2021.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are
  presented to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action:
  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  2
City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 7, 2021
   C. RESOLUTION NO. 21-63 REAUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE
  CITY’S COMMISSIONS TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY
  FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL
  361

  Resolution No. 21-63 makes findings that allow the City to continue
  implementation of teleconference/internet-based accessibility for public
  meetings under state-of-emergency provisions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-63 regarding
  the use of teleconferencing for public meetings.

  D. DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE COMPLIANCE REPORT REQUIRED
  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §66006 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-21

  Pursuant to Government Code §66006, a local agency which levies a fee
  subject to Government Code Section 66001 shall make a report available to
  the public with the information required by Government Code §66006(b)(1)
  and shall review that information at the next public meeting not less than 15
  days after the information has been made available to the public. The report
  was prepared in compliance with the applicable Government Code sections
  and hereby transmitted for City Council approval. The report was publicly
  available on the City’s website beginning November 22, 2021.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the attached Annual
  Development Impact Fee Compliance Report for Fiscal Year 2020-21 in
  accordance with Government Code §66006.

  E. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 21-49 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED
  SALARY SCHEDULE FOR PART-TIME LIMITED SERVICE POSITIONS TO
  INCORPORATE A SALARY INCREASE AND MINIMUM-WAGE
  ADJUSTMENT, EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2022

  On January 1, 2022, the State minimum wage will increase to $15.00 per hour.
  To maintain compliance with State minimum-wage law, staff recommends
  increasing the salary range of all part-time, limited-service position
  classifications and adoption of Resolution No. 21-49 authorizing the new
  salary schedule.
  Recommended Action:

  3
City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 7, 2021
   Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-49
  amending the City’s Authorized Salary Schedule for part-time/limited-service
  positions to incorporate the 4% salary increase and new minimum wage
  requirement, effective January 1, 2022.

  F. SECOND AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT WITH FIRST TRANSIT FOR DIAL-
  A-RIDE TRANSPORTATION SERVICES

  The City of San Gabriel contracts with transit provider, First Transit, to manage
  and operate its Dial-A-Ride service. In February, the City Council approved an
  amendment to the agreement with First Transit through December 2021. In
  October, the City Council directed staff to bring back an agreement with First
  Transit and RideCo for expanded transit services. This updated agreement to
  include a microtransit component is still being finalized. In order to maintain
  a current contract with First Transit, staff recommends that the City Council
  approve the Second Amendment to the Agreement with First Transit for
  continued service on a month-to-month basis at a monthly rate of $39,303.50
  through April 30, 2022.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Second Amendment to
  the Agreement with First Transit.

  G. 2022 LUNAR NEW YEAR FESTIVAL

  As part of the Fiscal Year 21-22 budget, the City Council allocated funding for
  community-engagement events. A portion of that funding is designated for
  the 7th Annual Lunar New Year Festival to be hosted by the City of San Gabriel
  on Saturday, January 29, 2022 from 11:00 A.M. to 7:00 P.M. in the Mission
  District. The City plans to work with Independent Contractor Linda Ngay to
  produce a unique Lunar New Year event for our community.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive the formal bid purchasing procedure requirement by separate
  motion; and
  2. Approve and authorize the City Manager to execute the Professional
  Services Agreement with Linda Ngay for $28,000; and
  3. Adopt Resolution No. 21-62 for the appropriation of $35,500 into account
  121-721-00-27-047.

  4
City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 7, 2021
   H. AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT TO ELECNOR BELCO ELECTRIC,
  INCORPORATED FOR INTERSECTION SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS AT FOUR
  CITY INTERSECTIONS

  This is a project funded through the Federal Highway Safety Improvement
  Program (HSIP) Cycle 7. The proposed project will install protected left-turn
  phases for the eastbound and westbound traffic at the intersection of Las
  Tunas Drive and Mission Drive and for the northbound and southbound traffic
  at the intersection of Las Tunas Drive and Del Mar Avenue. The Council will
  consider awarding the contract to the lowest responsive bidder, Elecnor Belco
  Electric, Incorporated a construction contract for Highway Safety
  Improvement Program (HSIP) Cycle 7-funded by the Federal Highway
  Administration to install protected left-turn phases at Las Tunas Drive &
  Mission Drive and Las Tunas Drive & Del Mar Avenue signalized intersections,
  and install rectangular rapid-flashing beacons (RRFBs) for the uncontrolled
  crosswalks at Las Tunas Drive & Country Club Drive and San Gabriel Boulevard
  & Live Oak intersections for an amount not to exceed $729,531.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-61 to appropriate $128,910 from Proposition C
  funds to account 122-800-50-97-103;
  2. Approve plans and specifications for the Cycle 7 Highway Safety
  Improvement Program, Contract No. 20-09;
  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a construction contract with
  Elecnor Belco Electric, Incorporated for a total bid amount of $729,531;
  4. Authorize the City Manager to approve a labor and material cost increase
  of $48,368; and
  5. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Elecnor
  Belco Electric, Inc. for an amount not to exceed $850,853 which includes a
  10% construction contingency.

  I. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH DUKE’S ROOT CONTROL,
  INCORPORATED FOR CITYWIDE SEWER LINE CHEMICAL ROOT CONTROL

  Under the Sewer Consent Judgment entered into by the City and the Regional
  Water Quality Control Board (RWQCB), San Gabriel is required to have a root
  control program in place. Roots are one of the leading causes of sewer
  system overflows (SSOs). Staff seeks to augment the current annual
  preventative-maintenance cleaning program with a chemical root-control
  agent used to hinder root growth. Staff is requesting the approval of a multi-

  5
City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 7, 2021
   year Professional Services Agreement with Duke’s Root Control, Inc. for
  citywide sewer line root chemical applications in the amount of $79,754.04,
  and authorize an additional 10% contingency amount of $7,975.40.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-60 to appropriate $55,729.44 from the Sewer
  Fund to account 137-800-01-22-000 (Sewer Contractual);
  2. Waive formal procurement process and authorize a sole source purchase;
  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a Professional Services Agreement
  with Duke’s Root Control, Inc. in the amount of $79,754.04 for citywide
  sewer main root foaming services and authorize $7,975.40 for a 10%
  contingency; and
  4. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order in an amount
  not to exceed $87,729.44, which includes a 10% contingency from account
  137-800-01-22-000.

  J. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH GOLDEN BELL PRODUCTS,
  INCORPORATED FOR CITYWIDE SEWER LINE ROACH CONTROL

  Under the Sewer Consent Judgment entered into by the City and the Regional
  Water Quality Control Board (RWQCB), San Gabriel is required to adopt and
  perform a complete sewer-maintenance program. Staff seeks to augment the
  current annual preventative-maintenance program with a chemical roach-
  control agent used to exterminate roaches. Golden Bell Products has the sole-
  source right for the application of Insecta, the only registered product of its
  type and with an active ingredient labeled for use in sewer manholes. Staff is
  requesting a multi-year Professional Services Agreement with Golden Bell
  Products, Inc. for four applications of chemical roach-control treatment
  service in an amount not to exceed $73,500.00.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-59 to appropriate $58,500 from the Sewer Fund
  to account number 137-800-01-22-000 (Sewer Contractual); and
  2. Waive the formal procurement requirements and authorize the sole
  source purchase;
  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a Professional Services Agreement
  with Golden Bell Products, Inc. in the amount of $73,500; and

  6
City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 7, 2021
   4. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Golden Bell
  Products, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $73,500.

  K. ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 21-60, AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO ENTER THE
  SETTLEMENT AGREEMENTS WITH OPIOID DISTRIBUTORS, AGREE TO
  THE TERMS OF THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING ALLOCATING
  SETTLEMENT PROCEEDS, AND AUTHORIZE ENTRY INTO THE
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE ATTORNEY GENERAL

  The City Council will consider adoption of Resolution No. 21-60, authorizing
  the City to enter the Settlement Agreements with McKesson Corporation,
  Cardinal Health, Incorporated, Amerisource Bergen Corporation, Johnson and
  Johnson, Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Incorporated, and Ortho-McNeil-Janssen
  Pharmaceuticals, Incorporated, agree to the terms of the Memorandum of
  Understanding allocating settlement proceeds, and authorize entry into the
  Memorandum of Understanding with the Attorney General.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council deliberate and adopt the Proposed
  Resolution if desired.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS – None.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

  12. ADJOURNMENT

MINUTES OF DECEMBER 7, 2021
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Liao called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 7:44 P.M.
  on Tuesday, November 16, 2021, at the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Liao.

  ROLL CALL
  Council Members Present:  John R. Harrington, Denise Menchaca, Jason Pu, Vice
  Mayor Tony Ding, and Mayor Chin Ho Liao.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  Police Chief Eugene Harris, City Attorney Keith Lemieux,
  Community Services Director Rebecca Perez, Chief City
  Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer
  Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human

I  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Finance Director William Kaholokula, Community
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  AN NOU NCEM ENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Liao announced that the agenda order was approved .

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  BALDWIN

I  Mayor Liao made the presentation.

  B. EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION AWARDS

  Police Chief Harris made the presentation .

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

   Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nunez, Chair of the Human Equity, Access, and Relations (HEAR)
  Commission, on behalf of the HEAR Commission, thanked City staff members who
  provided support for the Commission.

  Debbie Kilgore, resident, expressed appreciation for having an in-person City Council
  meeting, commended Police and Public Works Departments' management for making
  a big difference in the City over the last five years, and commended Chris Camacho of
  the Public Works Department for his responsiveness to her concerns.

I  Marsha Wood, resident, commended the Tree-Lighting Event and condition of the
  City's streets; questioned why Athens Services recycling is handled differently in the
  City than the County areas; and commented on differences in building requirements
  and permits between the City and County.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Chief City Clerk Clark announced that staff had requested that Items 4G and 41 be
  approved as amended:

  was amended to include language that was inadvertently omitted.
  •  Item 41, Professional Services Agreement with Duke's Root Control,
  Incorporated, for Citywide Sewer Line Chemical Root Control, the resolution

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Pu

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  Services and Public Wo rks Departments for a job well -done on the Tree-Lighting

I  Event; and wished all a Merry Christmas, Happy Holidays, and a Happy New Yea r.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Pu reported on a League of CA Cities Governing Board meeting;
  thanked all the employees, especially those who received awards; commented that the
  last five years of management has really made a difference that shows in the City, and
  wished all Happy Holidays.

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINU TES  Page 4 of 5  Dece mbe r 7, 2021
   Vice Mayor Ding reported on the Innovating Commerce Serving Communities (ICSC)
  Convention; congratulated Sally Baldwin and employees on their awards, wished all
  Happy Holidays, Merry Christmas, and Happy New Year.

  Council Member Menchaca congratulated everyone who received an award; thanked
  all the employees on the San Gabriel team, and Police Chief Harris for officiating the
  meeting; and wished all a Merry Christmas, Happy Holidays, and a safe and healthy

I  Council Member Harrington thanked all involved in putting on tonight's event and

  Mayor Liao announced that the regular meeting scheduled for December 21, 2021,

  In response to a question from Mayor Liao as to whether the next regular meeting
  would be held in person, Chief City Clerk Clark responded that staff is monitoring the

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:29 P.M .
